post.name: If humans colonize deep space, it would make sense to adopt metric time.
post.body:
The further we go from Earth and our Sun, the more Earth-based timekeeping begins to break down and becomes less useful as a concept, especially as generations pass. What matters it to Proxima Centauri how many times the Earth has revolved around its local star?

Metric time would provide a universal standard that doesn't depend on any reference to particular rotations and orbits of planets/star systems. Then each system and planet can have their own local timekeeping units, and metric time can enable easy conversions between them.

Using atomic clocks and taking seconds as the primary unit, here's what that could look like:

1 interstellar second = 1 earth second\
1 decasecond = 10 earth seconds\
1 hectosecond = 1⅔ earth minutes (1 interstellar minute)

1 kilosecond = 16⅔ earth minutes\
10 kiloseconds = 2.777 earth hours (1 interstellar hour)\
100 kiloseconds = 1.157407 earth days (1 interstellar day)

1 megasecond = 11.57407 earth days (1 interstellar week)\
10 megaseconds = 16.534391 earth weeks (1 interstellar month)\
100 megaseconds = 38.58024691 earth months (1 interstellar year)

1 gigasecond = 31.709791983764 earth years (1 interstellar decade)\
10 gigaseconds = 1 interstellar century\
100 gigaseconds = 1 interstellar millenium

post.name: You can now do everything that made you wish you were an adult as a child
post.body:
I suddenly realized it's been a while since I last filled the shower with loads of soap bubbles. When suddenly it hit me: I'm an adult, I can do whatever the hell I want.

So I did, I poured some body soap down and hit the water with the strongest jet mode our showerhead's got. It was amazing, I overfilled the rather shallow stand-up shower with tons of soap! Up to belly when sitting down!

The whole time, I was happy, giggling, playing with the soap which I carefully broke down into creamy fine bubbles through the otherwise long forgotten techniques which I just recalled. The only thing missing was a mirror so I could see my white soap hair and my big soap beard.

This shower thought hit at that very moment.

I had a knockoff dart shooting machine gun as a child, and I realized even though I am not a big adult gun fan, I still admire dart weapons a lot. Pulled out the ol' trusty, hooked its 6xAA battery holder to a power supply and let it go bam bam bam and brrrt.

I genuinely missed that thing, a lot.

I also realized that, as an engineering student and quite an experienced nerd, I got skills that weird 10yo machine lover fella could only dream of. It would be incredible if I could meet myself from the past and just nerd out with them.

And if you're looking for me, I'll be suping up a random RC car with a giant 24V motor and big road adhesion (?) fans. I always wanted to do something like that.

Its always fun to recall some childhood fun. Remember to do so once in a while...

post.name: I'll never forget how badly the term "AI" nosedived into being uncool
post.body:
Artificial intelligence, or AI, was once understood to refer to two things: science fiction robots, video game code made by humans to simulate NPC logic

It never referred to something lame. It was exciting, if maybe a scary concept that we could be glad wasn't real

Now, it's this... _thing_ this nuisance, this fucking thing that's everywhere, and it's also harmful and bad

And that's just depressing. It used to make you think of cool stuff. Now it just makes you think of sloprot

I remember when "no AI" meant one thing, and one thing only: modifying a Minecraft mob's NBT tag in Creative Mode

I was 12 or 13 years old, learning how to use Minecraft commands, and typing {NoAI:1} was the only time I had ever seen those two words put together

What's REALLY weird though, is that I actually had a weird thought. I was thinking to myself "lol imagine is NoAI was something that you complained about every day, like AAARRGGH NO AI" because that's just what the NBT tag made me think of. The absurd image of just some random fat guy in an air-conditioned home watching TV being like "no AI please" and I never could have guessed what that would have even meant. It was just me imagining hypothetical scenarios where the {NoAI:1} tag applied to everyday things that we had to toggle

And it's just... so so crazy, that in a way, my little kid self actually ended up predicting over a decade ago that we would one day be complaining about AI and being annoyed by it

post.name: Hey yall.  Please delete this if needed (I know this is the worst title ever)
post.body:
Hi this isn't so much a shower thought as a shot into the abyss so my apologies.  If you look at my history on here the only thing I do is post in shower thoughts for fun and I am not really someone that uses reddit, so this is more of a plea for some vague community I am aware of than a proper post here:

I am a 42 year old married man. I have certain mental disorders that do not allow me to live a normal life or leave me house.  So any kind of online interaction is unfortunately basically my only lifeline/connection to to the outside world other than my marriage (which is good really).  I'm just having a bit of a crisis because I wish so much that I could just be a normal person and be out in the world and do what I do.  I make music and art.  I will write a whole song and record every instrument, lyrics, etc and maybe upload it on a few of the usual social media platforms and get like maybe 2-3 likes total while I just seem to see the most vapid shit get tens of thousands of likes etc.  This is literally the whole point of this post. I have not much else to say about it. I get that it sounds stupid but again this is mainly how I can have any "social" interaction.  I'm literally crying while I post this and I *never* cry.  Just reaching out into the void like I said, so forgive me,❤️

Edit to say that I am not suicidal.

Second edit to thank anyone who commented.  This post *definitely* feels embarrassing, but I guess we all go through some shit sometimes.  Much love and I'll keep commenting my goofy shit here as usual.

post.name: Is GenAI the Problem I dont like to work anymore?
post.body:
Today, I am wondering if Generative AI is one of the reasons that I started feeling aimless in my job as a researcher.

I work a lot with data in various forms and in the process of data analysis and preparation, I have started to rely quite a lot on the use of LLMs to do tasks for me that would otherwise be tedious and but represented a large share in what i was doing before. Last week, I was tasked to understand, structure, and organise a complex administrative data set with bad documentation, and unclear temporal coherency to make it available for analysis. 

This would have been a challenging task some years ago. Maybe a week or two spent, focused on reading articles that have used the data set for other purposes, browsing documentation texts, looking up code bits on stackoverflow.

Instead, now, i bit by bit feed my instructions into an LLM trying to make sure it does the right things and provides the necessary documentation to keep the code sensible and human readable. But basically, I give a task, wait 20 minutes while the machine bobbles along, review what it had done, understand possible problems, set the next task, and then wait again.

In the in-between, I open a game of chess, or browse some articles (even interesting ones).

I can spend many hours like this, and usually finish the task quicker than i would have doing all the work by myself, or with an LLM of 3 years ago, where all code planning, and downloading was still done by hand, the LLM just helped me writing code blocks and syntax.

And I am wondering, if there is anything to do about this. Practically.

Because going back to the old world of doing 90 percent of the work (or even 100 percent), does not seem sensible from a pace perspective.

Yet, I also feel kind of empty while doing the task.

I am curious how other people have been in similar situation. 

(I would like to propose to not make this a conversation about the ecological or ethical downsides of GenAI. They are real and relevant, yet, maybe this conversation can be more about the personal experience of LLM use)
